_comment: US English abbreviation lexicon in two classes, same design as abreviacoes.pt.json (A-2). 'abbreviations' are proclitic: they introduce what follows and never close a sentence ('Mr. Smith', 'No. 5', 'Rep. Jones', 'Jan. 5', 'Brown v. Board'). 'unitAbbreviations' are enclitic units: they close a measurement and may close a sentence, so they only stop blocking the boundary when preceded by a number ('Sec. 2' blocks, '30 sec. Then' splits). Curated for the US federal register. Known limitations, declared rather than fixed: a sentence ending in 'no.' ('the answer is no.') does not split, because 'No. 5' is far more frequent in the register; 'Inc.', 'Co.' and 'et al.' closing a sentence do not split; 'p.m.' followed by a capitalized name splits. Common words that double as abbreviations ('art', 'sat', 'sun', 'in') are deliberately absent. Comparison is case-invariant.
